title: Arithmeticity of twisted finite correspondences for lattices over local fields
main_claim: Theorem 1 (Arithmetic exhaustion). Let Gamma be an ICC group commensurable with a lattice in a finite product of property-(T) simple groups over characteristic-zero local fields, and let Lambda be any countable ICC group, with arbitrary scalar 2-cocycles mu and omega. Then every bifinite L_mu(Gamma)-L_omega(Lambda) correspondence is a closed summand of a finite direct sum of models E(A,B,delta,sigma). Here delta: A -> B is an isomorphism between finite-index subgroups, and sigma is a finite-dimensional projective representation with multiplier mu/delta^*omega. In particular, Gamma and Lambda must be commensurable.

issues.location: Overall scope; Prop. 11.x (recovery-partition) combined with Lemma 1.x (compact-commutant reduction)
issues.description: This is not a defect, but the theorem is far stronger than the abstract suggests. In the weakly mixing reduced setting, the partition argument gives K ~= l^2(Gamma) (x) q_z K as a left module, so the left dimension is an integer. Together with the compact reduction and finite-index return, this gives three consequences. (1) The fundamental group of L(Gamma) is trivial for every lattice in the class, since an automorphism of an amplification gives a weakly mixing bimodule whose left and right dimensions would both have to be integers. (2) Stable Connes rigidity holds against an arbitrary ICC Lambda. (3) The same holds in all twisted variants. These settle long-open problems: Connes' problem on the fundamental group and the rigidity conjecture for higher-rank and Sp(n,1)/F4(-20) lattices. A claim of this size calls for extra scrutiny of the parts I did not verify line by line (Sections 4-8). I found no step there that fails.

issues.description: The coaxial/noncoaxial dichotomy uses paths 'in a common apartment' for two source vertices. A generic pair of boundary vertices together with the basepoint o does not lie in one apartment through o. The text recovers this through 'parabolic invariance to choose the split frames', i.e. conjugated split paths, which is plausible but only sketched. I could not turn this into a concrete failure.
issues.evidence: 'Choose paths t,a whose inverses tend to the two source vertices in a common apartment, using parabolic invariance to choose the split frames.' / 'Generic dual source vertices are opposite and hence coaxial'

coverage: Read in full and checked: the introduction and statement; Section 1 (twisted absorption, compact-commutant reduction including the Pimsner-Popa finite-dimensionality step, finite-index restriction and return, complementary regularity, induced algebras, product mixing); Section 2 (link identities and the isometry norm computation, relative boundedness, the no-bounded-stratum lemma, the full-flag amenability obstruction including the Kesten bound sqrt3/2, the strict-growth lemma, and the gap count); Section 3 up to and including type comparison (the transverse product estimate and fullness); Section 9, first 400 lines (the polynomial boundary kernel and the graph-domain identities); Section 10 from the reflection lemma onward (global commutation and chamber bijections); Section 11 in full (map space, uninduction, target transversal, deterministic partition through weak-mixing ergodicity, graph-model identification, exhaustion assembly). Skimmed: the openings of Sections 6 (the entropy lower bound and tight-factor lemmas checked), 7 and 8 (line normalization and moving tests). Checked by computer, using a custom Freudenthal multiplicity script: the optimal panel module table for SO(n,1), SU(n,1) and Sp(n,1), with c_R = k (7/2 for Sp(2,1) via the 14-dimensional primitive wedge^3) and d_R = 2 for SU(2,1) and Sp(2,1). Checked by hand: the restricted-root data (m_alpha, m_2alpha, Q) = (4n-4, 3, 4n+2) and (8, 7, 22), the sums of positive roots, Q > 8 and integrability of K^-2, and the model dimension formulas. Not read: Section 4 (finite panels), Section 5 (ray estimates), most of Sections 6-8, the rest of Sections 3, 9 and 10, and 00-models.
